title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended to be a single reference for employees and managers to understand required approvals, owners, thresholds, and operational steps.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to Redwood systems or representing Redwood for procurement / travel.
Exclusions: team-specific or project-level procedures that supplement these policies must be linked and will not override company policy unless explicitly noted.

Owners and escalation

- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team).
- Technical owner (access controls, RBAC): Security & Compliance.
- Procurement owner: Finance & Legal.
- Primary escalation path: immediate manager -> People Ops -> Security/Finance as appropriate.

Revision history

- 2026-02-01: Created (Asha Patel).
- 2026-03-04: Minor clarifications and added approval matrix (Asha Patel).

1) Access and Permissions

Purpose: ensure least-privilege access, auditable approvals, and timely deprovisioning.

Standards

- Principle of least privilege is enforced for all production and sensitive systems.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default model. Temporary exceptions may be issued as time-bound roles.
- All privileged access requires a documented approval and just-in-time (JIT) mechanism where possible.

Onboarding and offboarding

1. New hire access: manager files a ticket in the IT portal with the required systems and business justification.
2. Default new hire role: minimum necessary (network access, laptop build, email). Additional system access is granted via role requests.
3. Offboarding: manager must submit termination or transfer request in IT portal same day HR initiates departure. Security revokes SSO, VPN, cloud console, and admin privileges within 4 hours for terminated users and within 24 hours for voluntary departures.

Periodic reviews and audits

- Quarterly access review for all systems classified as sensitive.
- Annual audit of privileged accounts.
- Automated alerts for stale accounts (30 days of inactivity) and orphaned service principals.

Approval matrix (summary)

| Resource type | Approval required | Approver | Max duration (temporary) |
|---------------|------------------|----------|-------------------------|
| Production cluster (write) | Formal request + security review | Eng Manager + Security | 7 days |
| Production cluster (read) | Manager approval | Eng Manager | 90 days |
| Billing/finance console | Finance approval | Finance Manager | N/A |
| Vendor portal access | Vendor manager + Security | Vendor Owner + Security | 30 days |

2) Change Management

Purpose: maintain service reliability and reduce risk from configuration or code changes.

Change classification

- Standard changes: pre-approved, repeatable, low-risk (e.g., routine patching outside business hours).
- Normal changes: require change ticket, implementation plan, backout plan, testing, and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency changes: required to mitigate active incidents; must be logged and retroactively reviewed within 48 hours.

Process (normal change)

1. Open a change request (CR) in the change system including scope, impact, rollback plan, test plan, and runbook.
2. Peer review and owner sign-off.
3. Schedule a maintenance window and notify stakeholders (48 hours for non-critical services).
4. Execute change and perform smoke tests.
5. Record outcome and update the CR.
6. Post-change review for any change that caused service degradation or unexpected behavior.

SLOs and monitoring

- All normal changes must have a pre-declared SLO for acceptable post-change error budget impact.
- Automated monitoring and alerts must be verified before and after the change.

3) Data Management

Purpose: ensure data is handled securely, retained appropriately, and accessible to authorized users.

Data classification

- Public: safe to publish externally.
- Internal: company-internal documents, non-sensitive.
- Confidential: internal but limited to teams (e.g., design docs with PII redactions).
- Sensitive: customer data, billing, PII, or other regulated information.

Requirements by classification

- Access: Sensitive data requires two-factor (MFA) and RBAC-limited access.
- Storage: Sensitive and Confidential must be stored on approved encrypted services; production backups must also be encrypted at rest.
- Transmission: TLS 1.2+ required for data in transit.
- Retention: follow the retention schedule below.

Retention schedule (baseline)

- Logs: 90 days searchable, 2 years archived (compressed).
- Customer PII: retention by contract; default 7 years unless otherwise specified.
- Financial records: 7 years.

Data access request procedure

1. Submit data access request in the Data Portal with justification and data scope.
2. Data steward or owner reviews and approves or rejects within 5 business days.
3. If approved, request is issued with time-bound access and monitoring enabled.

Data breach and incident response

- Follow the Incident Response Security runbook (link in related pages).
- Notify Legal and Security within 1 hour of detection for Sensitive data exposures.

4) Procurement and Expenses

Purpose: provide a clear purchasing policy, approval flows, and expense reimbursement process.

Procurement thresholds and approvals

- Under $1,000: manager approval.
- $1,000 - $25,000: Dept head + Finance approval.
- Above $25,000: VP-level + Finance + Legal.
- Long-term contracts (>12 months) or contracts with vendor access to sensitive data require Legal review and Security assessment regardless of amount.

Vendor onboarding checklist (procurement)

- Completed vendor intake form.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed.
- Contract and NDAs signed by Legal.
- Finance setup for invoicing and payments.

Expense reimbursement (employee)

1. Submit expense via the corporate expense tool within 30 days of incurring the expense.
2. Attach receipts and business justification.
3. Manager approves; Finance processes payment within standard payroll cycle.
4. Exceptions: pre-authorized travel per travel policy.

5) Vendor Management

Purpose: ensure vendors are tracked, secure, and meet contract/service expectations.

Vendor lifecycle

- Selection: RFP/RFI when appropriate; Security completes risk assessment for vendors with systems access or data handling.
- Onboarding: vendor intake checklist (see procurement section).
- Monitoring: quarterly review of SLAs, access, and security posture for critical vendors.
- Offboarding: revoke all credentials, remove integrations, retain artifacts per retention policy.

Risk levels and controls

- Low risk: marketing, general supplies — minimal security checks.
- Medium risk: SaaS with limited data access — security questionnaire + SOC2 attestation requested.
- High risk: vendors with access to production or customer data — penetration test results, continuous monitoring, legal terms for data protection.

6) Travel Policies

Purpose: standardize business travel booking, expenses, and approvals to control costs and ensure safety.

Booking and approvals

- All travel must be booked through the company travel portal or approved travel agent unless pre-authorized.
- Domestic travel < $1,500: manager approval.
- International travel or travel > $1,500: Director-level approval.
- International travel to high-risk regions requires Security clearance and additional approvals.

Per diem and expenses

- Mileage, meals, lodging reimbursed per corporate expense policy. Receipts required for lodging and meals over $25.
- Non-refundable tickets are allowed only with manager approval.

Traveler safety and incident reporting

- Register travel itinerary with People Ops for international trips.
- In case of incident (medical, security), contact People Ops and Security immediately.

7) Internal Templates and Forms

Purpose: provide standardized templates to accelerate approvals and ensure auditability. Templates available in company drive include:

- Access Request (system role request) template.
- Vendor intake form and security questionnaire.
- Change Request (CR) template with rollback and test plan sections.

- Data Access Request template.
- Standard Contract Addendum for data processing (DPAs).
- Travel approval form and pre-authorization template.

How to use templates

1. Locate the template in the Templates folder on the company drive (link in related pages).
2. Fill required fields and attach supporting documentation.
3. Submit via the respective portal (IT, Procurement, Data Portal, Travel).

Exceptions and overrides

- Any exception to these policies must be documented and approved by the policy owner and an appropriate second approver (Security, Finance, or Legal depending on context).

Compliance and enforcement

- Non-compliance may result in access revocation, denial of procurement, or HR action depending on severity.
- Regular training: annual policy review required for all staff (completion tracked in People Ops).

FAQs (common questions)

Q: How fast will I get access for onboarding?
A: Typical SLA is 3 business days for non-privileged access; 7 business days for privileged/production access pending approvals.

Q: Who approves emergency changes?
A: The on-call owner plus a senior engineering director and Security must be notified; retrospective approval performed within 48 hours.

Appendix: Quick checklists

Onboarding checklist (short):
- Manager submits IT ticket with list of systems.
- People Ops creates employee record.
- Security provisions MFA + SSO config.
- Manager requests role assignments and documents justification.

Procurement checklist (short):
- Complete vendor intake form.
- Obtain Security questionnaire (if applicable).
- Legal signs contract/NDAs.
- Finance sets up vendor account.

Change rollout checklist (short):
- CR filed with rollback plan.
- Peer review complete.
- Stakeholders notified.
- Smoke tests defined.

End of document.
